summary: This is the farmers' market app with two stream pipelines updated: the vendor list is now deduplicated and alphabetized inside the pipeline, and the vendor menu is cut off after three items. It shows how sorting, deduplicating, and limiting are each just another step added to a stream.

lines.text: The variable is now a List<String> rather than a Set<String>, because the pipeline itself handles both the uniqueness and the ordering instead of relying on a collection type to force them.
This earlier pipeline was already sorting, comparing organic summer items by price from low to high exactly the way Comparator.comparing worked for collections in Chapter 8.
distinct() drops repeated vendor names as they flow through, playing the same role HashSet did in Chapter 7 but without creating a separate collection to hold them.
With no comparator supplied, sorted() uses the natural order of the elements, which for strings is alphabetical; the original products list is untouched.

This step is left commented out on purpose so you can see that order in the pipeline matters: sorting before the limit would give the three alphabetically first items instead of the first three found.
limit(3) stops the pipeline once three menu lines exist, which is what a vendor with a small display board needs.
